title: Orchestrate TF GPU shard reconciler and IAM broker for cross-VPC private installs
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: customers running Private deployments reported intermittent TF apply failures when tenant-scoped GPU pools were created concurrently across peered VPCs. Root cause summary: race between TF state writes and IAM role provisioning combined with non-deterministic subnet claims caused orphaned GPU nodepools and broken node affinity bindings. Goal: provide a robust TF-level orchestrator and an IAM 'broker' module that serializes cross-account role binding and performs an idempotent statebackfill/preflight verification before large apply rolls. This PR introduces: 1) a small orchestrator module (modules/tf_orchestrator) that runs a deterministic preflight plan, gathers remote state from configured state backends, computes a minimal set of patch operations, and emits a safe apply plan; 2) an iam-broker module (modules/iam_broker) that centralizes cross-VPC role creation, uses an explicit 'claim token' pattern, and supports a reversible rotation hook; 3) a gpu-shard module update (modules/gpu_pool) to expose shard keys and a stable subnet claim annotation so the orchestrator can reconcile leases; 4) migration helpers and a migration job template (examples/migrations/gpu_shard_backfill_job.yaml) to perform safe backfills in large fleets; 5) tests and CI glue to exercise corner cases. Checklist: [x] design doc attached (linear ENG-4123) [x] unit tests for tf modules [x] integration runner (kind+terragrunt) [x] migration plan and rollback steps documented [x] tagging/labels for runtime metrics. Commits summary: - init: add tf_orchestrator core scaffolding and README - add: iam_broker module with claim token resource and rotation hook - refactor: gpu_pool to export shard_key and subnet_annotation - feat: migration job and migrator script + example k8s Job manifest - test: add integration tests for preflight failures and repair - ci: add pipeline step to run orchestrator dry-run. Changed areas/files: modules/tf_orchestrator/main.tf, modules/tf_orchestrator/outputs.tf, modules/iam_broker/main.tf, modules/iam_broker/policy_templates.tf, modules/gpu_pool/variables.tf, modules/gpu_pool/outputs.tf, examples/migrations/gpu_shard_backfill_job.yaml, test/integration/test_orchestrator.sh, .github/workflows/integration-orchestrator.yml. High level diff notes: orchestrator adds a small statereader helper (uses terraform_remote_state and a lightweight python helper to compute desired->actual patches), iam_broker adds an aws_iam_role and a custom local-exec that emits a claim token to an S3 bucket with GPG envelope for cross-account verification, gpu_pool adds 'shard_key' index and 'subnet_claim_annotation' output. Testing: ran integration in CI that simulates two tenants racing to claim the same subnet; orchestrator dry-run detected conflicting claims and produced a deterministic serial plan; migration job successfully reattached orphaned nodepools in our test cluster. Review conversation: "Liam O'Connor: Why introduce a python helper inside TF modules? Can we keep logic purely in terraform?" || "Author (Maya): Terraform doesn't expose set-diff operations across remote states reliably; the helper is deliberately small (200 LOC) and documented; can be replaced later with a provider but we need a pragmatic fix." || "Wei Zhang: Please add more unit tests for rotation hook failure cases." || "Maya: Added tests and a fallback path that leaves an explicit tombstone tag to avoid silent drift." || "Arjun Rao: LGTM after CI green and a short security review for the GPG envelope usage." CI run history: first run failed due to an IAM policy lint (fix in commit 4), second run passed full integration. Merge: merged via squash on 2026-03-04 with merge commit message 'orchestrator: add tf gpu shard reconciler and iam broker (ENG-4123)'. Migration notes: release_notes: 'Adds a TF orchestrator and IAM broker to reduce race conditions when creating tenant-scoped GPU pools across peered VPCs. Operators should run the included migration job to reconcile existing orphaned leases; see examples/migrations for details.' Rollback plan: revert the module and run the reverse migration job which removes claim tokens and restores previous role bindings. Impact: non-breaking by default; new modules are opt-in via root module flags. Security: GPG envelope usage reviewed; secrets are not stored in cleartext, claim tokens are timebounded.

release_notes: Operators: run examples/migrations/gpu_shard_backfill_job.yaml to reconcile existing orphaned GPU leases. This PR adds an opt-in TF orchestrator and IAM broker to make future applies deterministic across peered VPCs. No automatic changes to existing installs will occur unless migration job is run.
additional_context: This approach is intentionally conservative: orchestrator performs a non-destructive dry-run first and emits a human-readable patch plan. The claim token pattern was chosen to avoid cross-account eventual-consistency races observed in our large fleet tests.
